Fixes from Opus review: #### **Blockers** * **Trusted Types sink names**: Updated sink names to use the declaring interface (`"ChildNode beforeHTMLUnsafe"`, `"ChildNode afterHTMLUnsafe"`, and `"ChildNode replaceWithHTMLUnsafe"` instead of `"Node ..."`). #### **Suggestions** * **DOM divergence note**: Added an explicit non-normative `

` under *parent for HTML insertion* explaining the intentional divergence from DOM `before()`/`after()`/`replaceWith()` regarding `template` and `Document` parents. * **`domintro` error descriptions**: Updated the `domintro` entries for all six positional methods to explicitly mention throwing `HierarchyRequestError` if the parent is a `Document` or `template` element. * **Helper invocation phrasing**: Standardized algorithm step invocations across all call sites to use `"the parent for HTML insertion given this"` and `"the HTML insertion target given target"`. * **Method alignment**: Aligned the step structure of `replaceWithHTML` and `replaceWithHTMLUnsafe` (binds `parent`, returns early if null, then invokes `filter and replace with HTML`). * **`[Unscopable]`**: Omission of `[Unscopable]` for the new `ChildNode` methods follows standard Web IDL practice (retained only for legacy identifiers for compat). #### **Nits** * **Helper parameter signatures**: Standardized to `a string html` and `data-x="tt-trustedparseroptions"` across `filter and set HTML`, `filter and pre-insert HTML`, and `filter and replace with HTML`. * **Formatting & Whitespace**: Fixed indentation (3 spaces) and line wrapping in *parent for HTML insertion*, closed missing `

` tags on `method steps are:

`, removed double spacing in algorithm signatures, and removed the stray extra blank line before the `Document.parseHTML` `domintro`.

> I don't understand something. Why are a lot of these methods only on `Element` and `ShadowRoot`? Why not have parity with the similarly-named DOM APIs?
> 
> I guess the problem is that we don't have a context element then?

Exactly... they have parity with `setHTML` and `setHTMLUnsafe` in that sense.

> `DocumentType` is called out above as gaining these `ChildNode` methods, however testing this, the new APIs don't actually work on `DocumentType` > > When attached its parent must be a `Document`, which causes `HierarchyRequestError`, and when detached it has no parent so these methods return early. > > ```js > let docType = document.implementation.createDocumentType("html", "", ""); > docType.replaceWithHTMLUnsafe("Example page"); > // throws a HierarchyRequestError > > const docType = document.implementation.createDocumentType("html", "", ""); > docType.parentNode; // null > docType.replaceWithHTMLUnsafe("

Hello

"); > // doesn't throw, but doesn't do anything as returns early > ``` > > Is that intentional and simply an acceptable consequence of matching the existing `ChildNode` API shape? Would it make sense to expose these methods via a mixin that only include `Element` and `CharacterData`, analogous to DOM's [`NonDocumentTypeChildNode`](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-nondocumenttypechildnode)? You're right, I'll move those methhods to `NonDocumentTypeChildNode`.

AI review Reviewed at whatwg/html#12753 031a042 and web-platform-tests/wpt#60555 0d5e8d9. **Suggestions** - `source:126217`: Renaming the heading changes its auto-generated anchor from `#html-parsing-methods` to `#html-parsing-and-insertion-methods`. That breaks existing links, including the `rel=help` in the new `positional-methods.html` and `positional-html-into-script-safe.html`. Consider `

`. - `source:126357-126521`: The long Trusted Types paragraph is copied into all six new `*HTMLUnsafe` domintro entries. With the existing two, that's eight copies to keep in sync. Consider having several `
`s share one `
`, or sending readers to the `setHTMLUnsafe()` entry for the TT behavior. - Commit message: It talks about "`ChildNode` methods" that are "also exposed on `CharacterData` and `DocumentType`". The IDL actually uses `NonDocumentTypeChildNode`, so the methods are not on `DocumentType`, and `positional-methods.html` checks exactly that. Consider fixing the wording. - wpt: No test checks that positional methods parse using the parent (or the host, for shadow roots and template contents) as context. Only the Safe script no-op covers this, indirectly. Consider tests like a `template.content` child calling `.afterHTMLUnsafe("x")` and checking the `td` is kept (context is `template`), and the same for a child of ``. **Nits** - `source:142916`: The line is 105 characters; rewrap it. - `source:127111-127126`: Two notes in a row cover the same divergence from the legacy methods; consider merging them. - `source:126466` (and the same text in the other two positional `*HTMLUnsafe` entries): "Otherwise, throws a `HierarchyRequestError`" follows the TT sentence, so it reads as if it only applies when TT isn't enforced. Consider "Then throws …", or putting it first like the Safe entries do. - wpt PR description: It links whatwg/html#12528, which is closed; the spec PR is #12753. - wpt `positional-methods.html:946-964`: The "on disconnected Element/Comment/…" tests are really about nodes with no parent. A disconnected node that has a parent wouldn't no-op. Consider "without a parent". - wpt `stream-html-with-trusted-types-createParserOptions-order.html`: When the stream test was moved here, it lost the old `recorded_type`/`recorded_sink` assertions. - wpt `positional-methods-with-parser-options.html:7` and `positional-methods-with-trusted-types.html:7`: These files are no longer tentative but still have `rel=help` pointing to WICG/declarative-partial-updates; point them at the HTML spec.

All addressed (here and in the WPT PR, including commit messages).

AI feedback Reviewed at 7944b13. Lint and the full build pass. Checked and fine: the IDL and method steps line up. Nothing can run author script between computing the parent or reference child and inserting, because Trusted Types runs first, so the pre-insert and replace calls can't throw. **Blockers** - [`html` element as parent](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127173-L127189): when the parent is an `html` element, it becomes the fragment parser's context. This happens for `document.body.beforeHTML()`, `document.head.afterHTML()`, and `document.body.replaceWithHTML()`. It also happens for `appendHTML()` and `prependHTML()` on `document.documentElement`, where the `html` element is the target. *Reset the insertion mode appropriately* then picks "before head", so the fragment always comes out as a `head` plus a `body`. For example, `document.body.beforeHTML("

x

")` inserts `

x

` before the existing body. The document ends up with two heads and two bodies, and `document.body` returns the new one. [`insertAdjacentHTML()`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127566-L127580) and [`createContextualFragment()`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127690-L127706) avoid this by parsing with a new `body` element as context. That doesn't carry over well here. With a `body` context, `document.body.replaceWithHTML("…")` drops the `body` start tag and leaves the document without a body. Throwing a "`HierarchyRequestError`" `DOMException`, as for a `Document` parent, may be the simplest fix. `setHTML()` on the `html` element is fine as is, since there a `head` plus a `body` is what you want. So the check would go in *filter and pre-insert HTML* and *filter and replace with HTML*. Whichever way this goes, the note under *parent for HTML insertion*, the domintro, and the tests need to cover it. Chromium's implementation (`FragmentParserConfig::ForContainer`) currently matches the spec here, so it would need to change too. - [Safe-mode `script` check](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127268-L127292): this moved into the exported *fragment parsing algorithm steps*, so that algorithm can return null again. The PR then adds Asserts to [`outerHTML`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127476), [`insertAdjacentHTML()`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127586), and [`createContextualFragment()`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127712) to cope. #12583 moved this check out of the exported algorithm before it landed, so on main it lives in *set and filter HTML*. Consider a non-exported wrapper instead (e.g., "parse HTML for insertion"). It would do the check and otherwise return the result of *fragment parsing algorithm steps*, and the three *filter and … HTML* helpers would call it. The exported algorithm then always returns a fragment, and the three Asserts and the "or null" in [its intro](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127264-L127265) go away. **Nits** - [`ShadowRoot`'s `setHTMLUnsafe()` entry](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L126487-L126488) says "in the same way as for *element*'s `setHTMLUnsafe()`". The eight new entries, e.g. [`appendHTMLUnsafe()`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L126501-L126502), say "for `setHTMLUnsafe()`". Pick one. - The six positional domintro entries, e.g. [`beforeHTML()`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L126415), link "template contents" but not "shadow root". Consider `shadow root`. - [Fragment scripting mode](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L142994-L142995): "(and the other HTML insertion methods)" includes the Safe methods, which never run scripts. Consider "the other `Unsafe` HTML insertion methods". - [*fragment parsing algorithm steps* intro](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127264-L127265): "are as follows. They return either a `DocumentFragment` or null:" doesn't match the "…are the following steps. They return …" pattern used elsewhere. This goes away with the wrapper above. - (optional) [Renaming *set and filter HTML*](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L127208) drops the `#set-and-filter-html` anchor, which mozilla/explainers and a couple of DOM implementations link to. `` keeps those links working, [as done elsewhere](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L1894). - (optional) The [mXSS paragraph](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/7944b13116f9304153d40be049d25b20fd6b56ee/source#L130609-L130613) says "`setHTML()` uses the current element". `beforeHTML()`, `afterHTML()`, and `replaceWithHTML()` use the parent (or its host) instead. - The PR title says "parsing", but the commit says "insertion". The squash commit takes the PR title. - Commit message: "a direct child of a `template` element is considered an invalid parent" reads as if the child is the invalid parent, but it's the `template` element. Also, "Renamed" → "Rename", to match "Add" and "Use". - (optional) Checklist: "Chromium: Implemented" has no link, and the MDN box is ticked without an issue.

> AI feedback

Throwing an exception when using those methods with an `html` parent. Also addressed the rest of the nits.
